note: PROC-12 merge driver can emit a confidently-WRONG generated artifact, and the merge still succeeds. Measured on The Stylus at the Stage 1 boundary, absorbing main into campaign/the-stylus. docs/audits/type-audit-report.md is registered to merge=hv-regenerate. After a merge that reported NO conflict at the command line, the committed artifact read hearsay 68 and identifier-text 736 -- byte-identical to OUR pre-merge side. origin/main held 70 and 735. The correct merged value is 737 and 70 (base 734, +2 from this branch, +1 from The Cupel on main), which existed on NEITHER side, so only regeneration produces it. The driver DID run: replaying the same merge with -c merge.hv-regenerate.driver=false conflicts on exactly that path, three stages in the index. So it was invoked, exited ZERO, and wrote ours-equivalent content -- meaning it regenerated from a tree that did not yet carry the other sides source changes. A zero exit is a successful merge, so nothing flagged it, and the drift check compares worktree to HEAD (both stale) and reports clean. WHAT SAVED IT: the post-merge hook advice to run make rebaseline. WHAT TO DO: always run make rebaseline after absorbing main and diff the declared paths, even when the merge was clean and even though a driver claims to own the file. Merging this branch without that step would have REGRESSED another campaigns committed artifact on main.
